items.item: Crow's foot diagrams represent entities as boxes and relationships as lines, with different shapes at the line ends representing relative cardinality

at.step: Reveal: the three symbols

items.item: Three symbols represent cardinality: the ring for zero, the dash for one, the crow's foot for many

at.step: Reveal: the three symbols

items.item: The symbols pair up: the inner component is the minimum, the outer component is the maximum, giving the four optional/mandatory, one/many combinations

at.step: Reveal: one-to-one — customer and loyalty card
Reveal: optionality changes the symbol, not the shape

items.item: A relational database requires a base table to resolve many-to-many relationships

at.step: Reveal: why many-to-many forces a junction table

items.item: A junction table maps two or more tables by holding a foreign key to each, with its own primary key typically composed of those foreign-key columns together
